question: As per Indian public healthcare delivery norms, a Primary Health Centre (PHC) in a hilly or tribal area is designed to serve a population of approximately:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A population of 20,000 applies to Sub-Centres in plain areas, not PHCs. The Sub-Centre is the lowest tier, covering 3,000–5,000 (hilly/tribal) to 5,000 (plains).

answers.text: 20,000 people (this IS the hilly/tribal norm for PHCs)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. For PHCs, the hilly/tribal norm is not 20,000. Review the five-tier pyramid: Sub-Centre → PHC → CHC → Sub-District → District.

answers.text: 20,000 (hilly) vs 30,000 (plains) — same as plains norm, just half

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The ratio is not 'half'. For PHCs: plains = 30,000; hilly/tribal = 20,000. For Sub-Centres: plains = 5,000; hilly/tribal = 3,000.

answers.text: 20,000 in hilly/tribal areas versus 30,000 in plains

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A PHC covers 30,000 population in plain areas and 20,000 in hilly, tribal, or difficult terrain areas — reflecting the lower population density and harder access in such regions.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review Park's textbook norms for the five-tier system. Key numbers: PHC serves 30,000 in plains and 20,000 in hilly/tribal areas; CHC serves 1,20,000 in plains.
Well done. Remember the full norm set: Sub-Centre (5,000 plains / 3,000 hilly), PHC (30,000 plains / 20,000 hilly), CHC (1,20,000 plains / 80,000 hilly).
